title: 年度四项验收与后续安排 · Four listening sections

transcript:
Section 1: Week 52 Listening: Annual Review and Next Steps

Mia: Hi, Daniel. Thanks for coming in. So, this is your annual review for the community learning centre. How do you feel the year went?
Daniel: Hi, Mia. Honestly, it was a busy year. I think I improved a lot in teaching, but I also made some mistakes.
Mia: That's normal. Let's look at the four areas: teaching, admin, teamwork, and professional development. First, teaching. You taught three evening classes this year. How did they go?
Daniel: The evening classes went well. Attendance was good, and most students passed their final test. But I think my instructions were sometimes too long.
Mia: Yes, I noticed that too. Short instructions are better. Now, admin. You were responsible for the weekly attendance records. Did you finish them on time?
Daniel: Not always. I was late with the records twice, in March and May. I'm sorry about that.
Mia: Okay, that's noted. For next year, we can set a reminder. Now, teamwork. You worked with two other teachers on the summer project. How was that?
Daniel: The summer project was great. We shared lesson plans, and I learned a lot from the others. But I sometimes didn't reply to emails quickly.
Mia: Right. Quick replies help the team. Finally, professional development. You attended two workshops this year. Which ones?
Daniel: I went to a workshop on classroom management and one on using videos in class. The classroom management one was very useful.
Mia: Good. So, overall, your teaching is strong, but you need to improve admin and email communication. For next year, I suggest you make a short checklist before each class. Also, try to reply to emails within one day.
Daniel: That sounds practical. Can I also get feedback from a senior teacher?
Mia: Yes, we can arrange that. I'll send you a form to fill in. And remember, the deadline for the next year's plan is June 30th.
Daniel: June 30th. Got it. Thank you, Mia.
Mia: You're welcome. Let's meet again in September to review your progress.
Daniel: Sounds good. I'll start working on the checklist right away.
Mia: Great. Also, don't forget to submit your self-assessment form by the end of this week.
Daniel: Okay, I'll do that. Thanks for the reminder.
Mia: You're welcome. See you in September.

Section 2: Year-End Review and Next Steps

Good morning, everyone. This is a simulated announcement for our community learning centre. I’m going to talk about the year-end review and what comes next. Please listen carefully and take notes if you like.

First, the year-end review will take place on December 15th. It will start at 9 a.m. and finish at 11 a.m. The review will be held in Room 204, not in the main hall as in previous years. Please arrive ten minutes early to sign in.

Second, there are four things we will check during the review. These are: your attendance record, your completed assignments, your progress test scores, and your speaking participation. Each area is important, but the speaking participation is often the one people forget. Make sure you have evidence of your speaking practice, such as a short recording or a signed log.

Third, after the review, you will receive a short report. The report will show your strengths and the areas you need to improve. You will get this report by email within one week after the review. If you do not receive it, please contact the office.

Fourth, we will offer a follow-up planning session on January 10th. This session is optional but strongly recommended. In the session, you can discuss your goals for the next term and choose new courses. The session will be online, and you will receive a link by email.

Now, let me give you some advice for the review. Many students make the same grammar mistakes again and again. For example, they forget to use the past tense when talking about last year, or they use 'he' instead of 'she' when referring to a female teacher. To help you, we have prepared a short checklist. The checklist has five points. You can download it from our website. Use it to check your own writing before the review.

The five points on the checklist are: 1) Check past tense verbs. 2) Check subject-verb agreement. 3) Check articles (a, an, the). 4) Check prepositions (in, on, at). 5) Check pronoun use (he, she, it, they). These are the most common errors we see.

Finally, remember that the review is not a test. It is a chance to see your progress and plan your next steps. If you have questions, please email the office. Thank you for listening.

Section 3: Week 52 Listening Part 3: Final Review and Action Plan

TUTOR: Good morning, Mia and Leo. This is our last tutorial before the exam. Let's review your progress and make a short checklist for the final week. Mia, can you start with the grammar points that still cause problems?
MIA: Sure. I still make mistakes with subject-verb agreement, especially when the subject is far from the verb. For example, I wrote 'The list of items are on the desk' instead of 'is'. Also, I sometimes forget to use the past perfect when talking about two past events. Like 'When I arrived, the film started' instead of 'had started'.
TUTOR: Good. Those are common. Leo, what about you?
LEO: I have trouble with articles. I often say 'I need advice' but then I say 'an advice' by mistake. And I mix up 'few' and 'a few'. Also, I sometimes use 'although' and 'but' together, which is wrong.
TUTOR: Right. So for the checklist, let's focus on three areas: subject-verb agreement, past perfect, and articles. Also, avoid double conjunctions. Now, let's talk about your listening and reading strategies. Mia, how do you handle multiple-choice questions?
MIA: I read the options first, then listen for keywords. But I sometimes choose an option that is mentioned but not correct.
TUTOR: That's a classic distractor. You need to listen for the whole meaning, not just words. Leo, what about matching headings in reading?
LEO: I read the headings first, then skim the paragraphs. But I often spend too much time on one paragraph.
TUTOR: Set a time limit. Now, let's plan the final week. I suggest you do one full practice test on Monday, then review your mistakes on Tuesday. On Wednesday, focus on grammar exercises. Thursday, practice speaking with a partner. Friday, review vocabulary. Saturday, rest. Sunday, light review. Any questions?
MIA: What about writing task 2? Should we practice more essays?
TUTOR: Yes, write at least two essays and get feedback. Also, check your use of linking words. Leo, you mentioned you sometimes overuse 'moreover'. Try to vary your connectors.
LEO: Okay. And for listening, should we listen to podcasts?
TUTOR: Yes, but choose ones with transcripts so you can check your understanding. Also, practice note-taking. Now, let's make the checklist. Mia, you write it down. Include: check subject-verb agreement, use past perfect for earlier past, check articles before nouns, avoid double conjunctions, read options carefully, manage time in reading, write two essays, vary linking words, listen with transcripts, and rest on Saturday.
MIA: Got it. I'll share it with Leo.
TUTOR: Good. Remember, the exam is on Monday next week. Good luck!

Section 4: Week 52 Listening Part 4: Final Review and Action Plan

Good morning, everyone. I hope you are all feeling focused and ready for the last stretch of the term. Today I want to talk about the final review for your academic writing course. This is our last session, so I will focus on the four areas you need to check before the exam. I will also give you a short action plan for the remaining week, so you know exactly what to do each day.

First, let's look at the four areas. The first area is grammar. Many of you still make the same mistakes. For example, you often forget the third-person -s, as in 'she write' instead of 'she writes'. You also confuse 'since' and 'for'. Remember, 'since' is used with a point in time, like 'since 2020', and 'for' is used with a period, like 'for three years'. Another common error is the misuse of articles. You say 'I am student' instead of 'I am a student'. These errors are small, but they affect your score.

The second area is vocabulary. You need to use academic words correctly. Don't just memorize long words; learn how to use them in sentences. For instance, 'analyze' is a verb, and 'analysis' is a noun. You should also avoid repeating the same words. Try to use synonyms, but make sure they fit the context.

The third area is structure. Your essays need a clear introduction, body paragraphs, and conclusion. Each paragraph should have one main idea. Use linking words like 'however', 'therefore', and 'in addition' to connect your ideas. But don't overuse them.

The fourth area is task response. Make sure you answer the question fully. If the question asks for your opinion, give it clearly and support it with reasons. Don't just describe the topic.

Now, let me give you a short action plan for the final week. On Monday, review your grammar notes and do the exercises on pages 45 to 50. On Tuesday, practice vocabulary from the academic word list. On Wednesday, write a full essay under timed conditions. On Thursday, review your essay and check for the four areas. On Friday, take a rest and do light review. On Saturday, do a final mock test. And on Sunday, relax and prepare your materials for the exam.

Remember, the exam is on Monday next week. Good luck with your preparation.

grammar.title: 常见错误整理：时态与时间表达
grammar.explanation: 在英语中，描述过去发生的事情要用一般过去时，如“I was late”而不是“I am late”。另外，时间介词要准确：具体月份前用in（in March），具体日期前用on（on June 30th）。检查单上要提醒自己：过去时动词形式、时间介词、以及简短指令。
grammar.example: I was late with the records twice, in March and May.

options: I am late for the meeting yesterday.
I was late for the meeting yesterday.
I late for the meeting yesterday.
I were late for the meeting yesterday.
answers: I was late for the meeting yesterday.
questions.explanation: yesterday表示过去，主语I应用was，因此第二句正确。
